     leans toward the edge of getting wet.

     First comes the smell — that mineral hush,
     the scent of stone about to drink,
     a promise breathed across the roofs
     before a single drop can sink.

     Then one. Then two. A scattered tap
     on window glass and garden shed,
     like fingers practicing a scale
     across the shingles overhead.

     And then the whole world opens wide
     and rain comes down in silver sheets,
     a thousand rivers
